title: Split-Brain Consensus for Private Routing — Arch Review Notes
summary: Design discussion and decisions for preventing split-brain during regional network partitions in Private deployments. Focused on control-plane vs runtime failover, lease/heartbeat design, and safe routing fallback when clusters diverge.
background: Customers running Private across multiple on-prem clusters or VPCs can observe divergent model routing state during partial control-plane connectivity loss. Current heuristics (last-seen leader, tombstones) have produced two classes of failures: temporary double-routing (requests hitting two different model versions) and sticky stale routing that requires manual intervention. We need a predictable, automatable approach that minimizes user-visible flakiness while respecting data locality and tenant isolation.
agenda: Present proposed consensus-lite protocol for runtime routing decisions
Evaluate tradeoffs with existing lease/heartbeat and central control-plane approaches
Decide on short-term mitigations and long-term RFC scope
discussion_notes: INC summary: control-plane partial outage between region-a and region-b for ~8 minutes. Two private clusters accepted route updates independently; some heavy tenants experienced model mismatch causing inference variance in multi-region failover tests.

Problem statement refined: split-brain arises when both control-plane and peer-to-peer exchange are degraded and local runtime instances independently decide to promote local routing changes without deterministic reconciliation.

Proposal 1: Deterministic ranked-lease + monotonic routing tokens. Each cluster holds a soft lease with (lease-holder-id, epoch, monotonic-token). On partition, only higher epoch wins. When connectivity restores, monotonic-token ensures idempotent reconcile. Pros: simple, low-latency. Cons: relies on reasonably synchronized epoch increments and safe lease refresh/expiry tuning.

Proposal 2: Gossip-based partial-quorum confirmation. Runtimes gossip proposals and require quorum of region peers for promotion. Pros: stronger safety. Cons: increased latency and cross-region traffic (bad for private/offline networks).

Proposal 3: Control-plane-signed route assertions. Control plane issues signed route assertions with TTL and nonces; runtime accepts only signed assertions or fallback to read-only routing. Pros: cryptographic authority. Cons: central control plane still single point during partition unless multi-control-plane signing available.
SRE concerns: any approach increasing cross-cluster chatter must be opt-in for on-prem customers. Need to be able to toggle behavior per-tenant and per-deployment (air-gapped vs fully connected).

Performance note from serving-runtime: runtime can enforce fast local checks (<5ms) to detect divergent routing when KV-version drift observed and mark sessions as 'degraded' for short duration to trigger safe fallback policies.
Product constraints: must preserve privacy guarantees (no tenant data leaked across clusters) and allow customers to opt for strong safety over availability or vice versa.
Operations ask: provide a 'reconcile audit' log that records accepted route assertions, source of truth, and reconciliation actions for customers to view in Private Console.

Short-term mitigation discussed: implement 'safe-fallback mode' in runtime (30s) where on ambiguous state the runtime serves from pinned previous artifact and returns a specific response header indicating degraded routing to help debugging.

Long-term RFC scope: consensus-lite protocol that composes signed assertions from reachable control-plane replicas and local lease epochs, with opt-in gossip for connected deployments. Requires new route assertion protobuf and reconciliation API.

Security note: signed assertions must be verifiable offline; proposed to reuse existing KMS/HSM-backed signing keys per deployment; rotate keys with grace period to avoid false rejections during rotation.
decisions: Adopt a phased approach: implement short-term runtime 'safe-fallback mode' immediately (T+2 weeks) to reduce customer impact during ambiguous routing.
Proceed with RFC for consensus-lite model that combines control-plane-signed assertions plus local epoched leases. RFC to include opt-in gossip extension for fully connected private deployments.
Require reconcile-audit logs be surfaced in Private Console and included in incident bundles for customer-facing postmortems.
Make the new protocol opt-in per-deployment; default behavior for air-gapped installs remains conservative (favor availability with pinned artifacts).
tradeoffs: Safety vs latency: quorum or gossip increases decision latency; epoch/lease approach favors low-latency but requires careful expiry tuning.
Centralization vs autonomy: signed assertions centralize authority; local leases decentralize but risk divergence.
Operational complexity: opt-in per-deployment increases testing surface and adds config overhead for customers and SEs.
open_questions: Key management during key rotation: what is the safe window to accept assertions signed by both old/new keys? (action: security to propose rotation policy)
Lease expiry tuning: what default lease TTLs are safe across typical on-prem latency distributions? (action: infra to run sim)
Audit volume: how large will reconcile-audit logs be for customers with thousands of tenants? (action: observability to estimate storage/retention)
Gossip opt-in API: what API surface is acceptable for air-gapped customers to enable peer exchange? (action: private-deployments to draft)
Migration story for existing customers mid-rollout: how to transition without causing churn of routing state? (action: product + solutions eng)
